sentences.text: The present application has been filed seeking suspension of sentence during the pendency of the appeal.

By way of the present appeal, the appellant has assailed the judgment of conviction dated 14.02.2024 and the order on sentence dated 01.05.2024, passed by the ASJ-01 (POCSO), North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi, whereby he was convicted for offences punishable under Sections 363/376(2)(i)/174A IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

sentences.text: 1 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the prosecution case rests primarily on the testimony of the prosecutrix, which is she claims suffers from contradictions and is inconsistent.
4. Learned APP for the State, on the other hand, opposes the application and submits that the victim was a minor aged about 12 years at the time of the incident.
The DNA report conclusively established that the appellant was the biological source of the semen found on the samples collected from the victim's private parts.
Further, the MLC notes the hymen being torn.

5. A perusal of the record reveals that the Trial Court, after a detailed analysis of the testimony of the victim and other prosecution witnesses, as well as the FSL/DNA report, found the charge under Sections 376(2)(i) IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act duly proved.
The reasoning adopted by the Trial Court is based on corroborated scientific evidence.

6. As per the nominal roll on record, the appellant has undergone a period of 03 years, 03 months,
and 15 days of imprisonment, including the undertrial period, and earned a remission of 02 months and 26 days. The unexpired portion of his sentence is 09 years, 06 months, and 19 days as on 15.04.2025.
7.
Keeping in view the testimony of the child victim, the corroborative DNA evidence, and the nominal roll of the appellant, no ground to entertain This is a digitally signed order.

8. The application is accordingly dismissed.
1. At this stage, learned counsel appearing for the victim states upon instructions that the entire compensation awarded by the Trial Court has been received by the victim.
2. List the appeal in due course.
